relevance_note: Narrative review of off-label canakinumab that summarises previously published Majeed syndrome patients with individual-level detail, e.g. "two brothers with Majeed syndrome" and "an American patient found to be compound heterozygous".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON and the 20-item checklist rows (all 'not reported', since the paper addresses none of the checklist items for these people in checklist terms). In-scope people come from the Majeed syndrome paragraph of 'Monogenic autoinflammatory diseases': the two brothers attributed to Herlin et al. (17), the compound heterozygous American patient (11) and the patient with dyserythropoietic anemia (33). The gene is tied to these patients only by the general sentence 'caused by mutations in LPIN2'; a variant row ('not reported' description) was created only for ref (11) patient, whose zygosity is stated; no variant rows for the others. Contradictions: Table 1 lists 'Herlin et al. (17)' as 1 female Majeed syndrome patient on 2 mg/kg/8 weeks, while the text says Herlin et al. (17) treated two brothers with 4 mg/kg/4 weeks; Table 1 lists 'Kisla Ekinci et al. (16)' as 2 male Majeed syndrome patients on 4 mg/Kg/4 weeks, but reference 16 and the text describe a DADA2 patient; Table 1 lists 'Haviv et al. (22)' as 2 females with 'CRMO/Majeed syndrome', while reference 22 and the text describe a boy with FOP; Table 1 lists Bhuyan et al. (11) as 1 male with DIRA, while the text cites (11) for an American Majeed syndrome patient. Because Table 1 rows are per study (not per patient), are misattributed, and probably describe the same people as the text, no individual rows were created from Table 1; sex was taken from the text ('two brothers') and left 'not reported' for ref (11) and ref (33) patients. 'dyserythropoietic anemia' was recorded as an observed feature but the checklist item 'dyserythropoiesis on bone marrow' was left 'not reported' because no bone marrow finding is stated. 'bone lesions on MRI' (resolution after treatment) was recorded as observed; CRMO was not marked because the paper does not call these lesions CRMO for these patients.
